**Historian: archive check on the Day 10 window**

My source contains no "Desync", sync offset, latency, hulpslag, or throughput figure, and none of the ENG-xxx IDs the Engineer cites. I cannot verify ENG-011, ENG-012, ENG-029, ENG-062, ENG-107 or ENG-120 from the archive. The nearest records I hold are below.

**(1) Baseline before Day 8:** None. There is no sync, latency, or message-arrival measurement for any date before Day 8. Related context only: HIS-006 (datanet connected to the Kroonklok 23 years ago), HIS-105 (woudkabels laid then, never changed), HIS-014 (Day 3 inspection, "niets gewijzigd"), and HIS-106 (no recorded hapering of the leylijnen in 23 years of datanet).

**(2) Earlier occurrences:** None for "half aangekomen" or sync offset. No packet loss on poort oost is recorded. The only poort oost loss entry is HIS-053 (Day 22, 04:15, "lek bij poort oost gemeld door de wachters, 3 minuten"). It describes a reported leak, filed under *schilden*, not packet loss.

The same-window Day 10 records are HIS-035 ("de Burchtader stokte even", gebeurd dag 10 04:45) and HIS-036 ("berichten half aangekomen", gebeurd dag 10 04:50). My archive places them together but does not link them causally.

I also must correct HIS-114, my own earlier entry, which called this a return of the Stille Winter. That was an analogy, not evidence. HIS-107 says the Stille Winter began without warning and that no datanet existed then, so it is not a sync precedent.

**Timestamp integrity:** HIS-036 has vastgelegd dag 9 23:55, before its gebeurd time. HIS-053 has vastgelegd dag 22 01:50, before its gebeurd time of 04:15. Clerk timestamp errors are recorded in HIS-112 (day 10) and HIS-116 (day 22). Treat these times as provisional.

**(3) Sync interval or recurrence:** None. No archived rule gives an interval or recurrence pattern. The only charter articles on the pols are:
- HIS-109, article 1: "Alles wat op de Kroonklok loopt, loopt op zijn ene pols. Een tweede pols ernaast brengt het uit de maat."
- HIS-110, article 2: a record written on another pols can be read only there, and if that pols drops, the record is lost. Before restoring the maat, make a copy of the register, then bring the pols together slowly.

HIS-102 states that the Kroonklok has one pols carrying the leylijnen, schilden, archive and datanet. HIS-110 is a remediation rule for any second pulse, not a timing rule.
